chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindy, from Ja'far ibn Bashir al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whenever there is a delay in the birth of a child for any of you, let him say:

'O Allah! Do not leave me alone while You are the Best of Inheritors, isolated and frightened, so that my gratitude falls short of my reflection. Rather, grant me a truthful posterity — males and females — through whom I find comfort from loneliness and tranquility from isolation, and I thank You for the completion of the blessing. O Endower! O Magnificent! O Exalted One!'
'Then grant me, in every good health, gratitude until You bring me through it to Your pleasure, in truthful speech, fulfillment of trusts, and faithfulness to the covenant.'

key_terms.الْعَهْد: The covenant — in Shia context often refers to the covenant of wilayah (allegiance to the Imams)
key_terms.الْوَحْدَة: Isolation — being alone, particularly in old age
key_terms.الْوَحْشَة: Loneliness/desolation — the emotional distress of being without children or companions
key_terms.رِضْوَانَكَ: Your pleasure/satisfaction — the ultimate goal of all worship
key_terms.عَاقِبَةَ صِدْقٍ: Truthful posterity — righteous children who are a source of lasting good

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for those who are delayed in having children?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a specific supplication for those experiencing difficulty in having children. The du'a echoes the Quranic supplication of Prophet Zakariyya (21:89) and asks God not to leave one alone and childless. The supplication culminates not merely in asking for children, but connecting that blessing to higher virtues: truthful speech, fulfillment of trusts (amanah), and fidelity to the covenant (al-'ahd) — understood in the Shia tradition as wilayah (allegiance to the Imams).
